full_judgment:
Contemner No. 1 Mr. Md. Shahjahan is the Assistant Judge at Monirampur Upazilla; contemner No. 2 Monirul Islam and eontemner No. 3 Nuruzzaman are Nazir and process server respectively of the Court of Assistant Judge at Monirampur and contemner No. 4 Omar Ali Mohaldar is a decree holder in the Ease No.1 of 1987-88 of  Monirampur Village Court. 

 2. The fact giving rise to the Rule for contempt is that decree holder opposite party contemner No.4 filed Title Execution Ease No. 1 of 1988 in the Court of the Assistant Judge praying for execution of the decree dated 30.8.87 passed in the said Ease No. 1 of 1987-88 by a Village Court ordering to evict the petitioner from a shop. Petitioner Ayub Ali Mohaldar opposed it and filed a petition before the Assistant Judge and prayed for quashing the Execution Ease. The said prayer was rejected by the Assistant Judge by his order dated 5.2.89 and he fixed 10.4.89 for execution. 

 3. The petitioner Ayub Ali, thereafter, filed a Civil Revision in this Court against the above order of the Assistant Judge dated 5.2.89 and obtained a Rule on 9.11.89 calling upon the decree holder Contemner No. 4 to show cause why the said order dated 5.2.89 passed by Assistant Judge in Title Execution Ease No. I of 1988 shall not be set aside and pending hearing of the Rule all further proceeding in the said Title Execution Ease No. I of 1988 was stayed. The order of rule and stay was passed around 11-00 AM and the petitioner's learned Advocate Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim issued a certificate to this effect on the printed pad of the Bar Association of this Court which is quoted below: 

 12. With regard to the contemner No. 1, the Assistant Judge, we find that the learned Lawyer for the petitioner, Mr. M A Rahim issued a certificate under his signature in a letter head with a seal of the Bar Association of this Court. The certificate was issued on 9.4.89 and an application was submitted before the Court of the contemner No. 1 informing him about the issuance of the rule and stay by this Court in the Execution Ease No. 1 of 1988. On that day no order was passed on this application. It is on record of the Assistant Judge that this application did reach his office in the afternoon of 9.4.89. Again on 10.4.89 at 9-30 AM another application was filed by the petitioner through his lawyer Mr. Arun Kumar Bhattacharjee and in that petition also the fact of issuance of rule and stay by this Court was mentioned and it was further stated in that petition that if the contemner Assistant Judge granted time upto 4-00 PM as prayed for, the petitioner would produce a certified copy of Rule and stay of this Court. From the order No. 24 dated 09.04.1989/10.04.1989 we find that the Assistant Judge received this application to recall the writ of execution. He, however, stated that the petition did not contain the signature of the petitioner and that no copy of the application was served upon the decree-holder. Then again on 10.4.89 in his Order No. 25 he stated that there was no number of the civil revision ease and, therefore, the contents of the application are not believable. Accordingly, he rejected the prayer to recall the writ of execution. The writ was executed by ejecting the petitioner from the shop and installing contemner No. 4 therein.
